investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every agent pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled for 130–146 seconds. The scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules, so no node can accept a new remote-agent pod. Because no VM is ever assigned, the eval probe never receives a vmId or a remoteState value, causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect, and the evidence is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact beyond the observability eval is unconfirmed.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 146s, confirming the condition persisted across a second independent probe attempt.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 144s, confirming the condition persisted across a third independent probe attempt.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-assignment step because the pod never started.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=135609, endedAt=2026-07-17T00:38:36.548Z — the probe ran for ~135s before timing out, which matches the scheduler message 'pod stuck unscheduled for 130s'.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, meaning VM scheduling is the first blocking step before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: the contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are in use by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, reducing the effective pool to those 2 nodes. If those rules are overly narrow or point to a node label that has changed, the effective capacity is artificially constrained.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster may be insufficient for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability — a prior eval run or leaked agent pod may be holding VM slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883) is intended to prevent this, but a failed cleanup from a previous run could leave orphaned pods consuming slots.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the production Kubernetes cluster immediately to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot usage on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes. If all slots are consumed, identify which workloads are holding them and whether any are orphaned or stuck.

Search for any pending or running remote-agent pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs. Terminate any orphaned pods to free slots.

If slots are legitimately consumed by production workloads, assess whether the 2-node affinity-eligible pool has sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity for concurrent production use plus eval probes. Consider increasing the slot limit on existing nodes or expanding the affinity-eligible node pool.

Review the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod template to determine whether the restriction to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional. If additional nodes could be made eligible by adding the required label, this would increase the scheduling pool.
Once the scheduling issue is resolved, re-run the eval to confirm that vmIdPresent and remoteState evidence is produced and the contract passes.

This is an eval-layer failure with no user-traffic or incident signals in the supplied evidence. Do not escalate as a confirmed user-facing outage until cluster inspection confirms the scope of the capacity exhaustion.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be identified.

If the eval probe succeeded (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]) on an immediate re-run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod was found to match more than 2 nodes, the '4 node(s) didn't match' count would be inconsistent with the current cluster state and the affinity hypothesis would need revision.

If a different error message (e.g., API authentication failure, network timeout, or application-level error) appeared on re-run instead of the Unschedulable scheduler event, the root cause would shift away from infrastructure scheduling.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the cause would be a missing resource registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add an eval or verifier probe that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each eligible node before attempting agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure signal rather than a downstream agent-creation timeout.

Add a pre-flight eval that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available on an affinity-eligible node before the remote-agent-create probe runs, enabling faster diagnosis and avoiding the 130s+ timeout.
Add an orphaned-pod cleanup eval that detects any remote-agent pods in Pending or Unknown state older than a configurable threshold and flags them as a capacity leak risk.

Consider adding a cluster-capacity check to the remote-agents feature group that monitors kata.peerpods.io/vm headroom and warns before it reaches zero, providing earlier signal than a full scheduling failure.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T00:38–00:43Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable with the message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905, createAgent call) cannot obtain a running agent pod, so it times out and returns no evidence, causing the contract validation to report all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) as missing.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every agent pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled for 130–146 seconds. The scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules, so no node can accept a new remote-agent pod. Because no VM is ever assigned, the eval probe never receives a vmId or a remoteState value, causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect, and the evidence is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact beyond the observability eval is unconfirmed.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly names resource exhaustion on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource as the blocking condition.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 146s, confirming the condition persisted across a second independent probe attempt.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 144s, confirming the condition persisted across a third independent probe attempt.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-assignment step because the pod never started.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=135609, endedAt=2026-07-17T00:38:36.548Z — the probe ran for ~135s before timing out, which matches the scheduler message 'pod stuck unscheduled for 130s'.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, meaning VM scheduling is the first blocking step before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: the contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are in use by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, reducing the effective pool to those 2 nodes. If those rules are overly narrow or point to a node label that has changed, the effective capacity is artificially constrained.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster may be insufficient for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability — a prior eval run or leaked agent pod may be holding VM slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883) is intended to prevent this, but a failed cleanup from a previous run could leave orphaned pods consuming slots.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the 6-node cluster has no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and that 4 of those nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's affinity or selector at all, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck in Unschedulable state for 130–146 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing any agent lifecycle step from executing and producing zero evidence output. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no room for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are categorically excluded from scheduling remote-agent pods, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 nodes and making the cluster more susceptible to VM slot exhaustion.

Tertiary — a prior eval or workload run that did not clean up its remote-agent pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new pods from being scheduled. The eval runner uses withCleanup (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1916), but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, leaked pods could be consuming slots.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of any remote-agent check that produces a scheduled pod and non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) would indicate the resource exhaustion was transient rather than persistent.
kubectl describe node output showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes would suggest the scheduler message was stale or the resource accounting is incorrect.
Evidence that the pod's node affinity or selector was recently changed to exclude more nodes, shifting the root cause from resource exhaustion to a misconfiguration regression.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state (the required sibling checks) while remote-agent-runtime continues to fail would suggest the failure is isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling constraint.
Cluster autoscaler logs showing that a scale-up event was triggered and completed between eval runs would indicate the capacity issue is self-healing.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, and emits a warning or skip result if headroom is below a threshold.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-Running for remote-agent pods and warns when scheduling latency exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s), surfacing capacity pressure before it causes full eval failures.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods in non-terminal states older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures from prior eval runs.
Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, alerting when the schedulable pool shrinks unexpectedly.
